title: Why World War I still matters: four empires, one shot

segments.text: In 1914, four empires ruled much of Europe and the Middle East.
The German, the Austro-Hungarian, the Russian, and the Ottoman.
Four years later, all four were gone.
Empires that had seemed permanent for centuries vanished in a few short years.
Out of their ruins came new countries: Poland, Czechoslovakia,
and Yugoslavia, the South Slav state that Princip's movement dreamed of.
Borders were redrawn, often in ways people resented.
The map of Central Europe and the Balkans still carries those lines.
Those resentments helped bring another world war within a generation.
Roughly nine to ten million soldiers had died.
